findings.title: Client/role/group removal fails when both FGAP v1 and v2 features are enabled
findings.body: The provider-event listener is now only executed when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` (v1) is enabled, but inside it still calls `management(session, realm)`, which returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` as soon as `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled (see `AdminPermissions.management`). With both features enabled, `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` handling calls `clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)` which in the new `ClientPermissionsV2` throws `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. The result is that deleting any client (and, via the same path, deleting roles/groups once those evaluators get V2 implementations) aborts with a server error and a rolled-back transaction. The event handler must pick the v1 implementation explicitly (or the v2 class must tolerate the call).

findings.title: V1 client management-permission endpoints break whenever the V2 feature flag is on
findings.body: `MgmtPermissionsV2` is selected purely from the global `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` feature flag, not from `realm.isAdminPermissionsEnabled()`. Consequently, for every realm in the installation (including realms that only use the v1 fine-grained admin permissions), `clients()` now returns `ClientPermissionsV2`, whose `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`, `managePermission`, `configurePermission`, `viewPermission`, `mapRoles*Permission` all throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. The admin REST endpoints `/admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id}/management/permissions` (GET and PUT) and the corresponding console screens therefore return HTTP 500 instead of working or returning a clear error. These methods should either delegate to the v1 behaviour when the realm does not have FGAP v2 enabled, or throw a mapped exception (e.g. `BadRequestException`/`ModelValidationException`) with a meaningful message.

findings.title: canExchangeTo throws UnsupportedOperationException, breaking token exchange
findings.body: `canExchangeTo` is invoked from the token-exchange flow (`AdminPermissions.management(session, realm).clients().canExchangeTo(...)`) independently of whether a realm uses fine-grained admin permissions. Because `MgmtPermissionsV2` is chosen based on the global `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` feature flag, enabling that feature makes every client-to-client token exchange hit this `UnsupportedOperationException` and fail with HTTP 500 instead of being allowed/denied. Either implement the check (deny/allow explicitly) or fall back to the v1 implementation when the realm does not have FGAP v2 enabled.

findings.title: No migration for realms that already have the admin permissions client: new scopes and Clients resource are missing
findings.body: `init()` creates the authorization scopes (`configure`, `map-roles-client-scope`, `map-roles-composite`, ...) and the per-resource-type "all resources" resource only once, when the admin permissions client is first created, and returns early if the client already exists. Realms that enabled FGAP v2 before this change therefore have neither the new scopes nor the `Clients` resource. In such realms: (1) `getOrCreateResource` for a client permission hits `scopeStore.findByName(...) == null` and throws `ModelException("No scopes found.")` (HTTP 500 on permission creation), and (2) `hasPermission(scope)`/`getResourceTypeResource` always return false/null so all-clients permissions can never be granted. A migration/upgrade step that adds missing schema scopes and resource-type resources to existing admin permission clients is needed.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission never returns client ids and leaks the aggregate "Clients" resource name
findings.body: `resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` only matches resources whose `type` is set to `Clients`. Per-client resources are created by `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` via `resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, owner)` which never sets the resource type, so individual client resources are never visited. The only resource with that type is the aggregate resource named `Clients` (created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.init`), so the method returns either an empty set or the literal string `"Clients"`, which callers interpret as a client id. Any caller relying on this contract (set of client ids the caller has the scope for) gets wrong results; no test covers it.

findings.title: Possible NullPointerException when the Clients resource-type resource cannot be resolved
findings.body: In `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, when no per-client resource exists the code falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`, which returns `null` when the realm does not support the authorization schema (e.g. `realm.isAdminPermissionsEnabled()` is false while an admin-permissions client still exists) or when the `Clients` resource has not been created (realms created before this change). The returned value is used immediately in `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` and, if that does not blow up, in `resource.getScopes()` on line 224, producing a NullPointerException / HTTP 500 during an authorization decision. The null case must be handled by returning false.

findings.title: getResourceName not extended for the new Clients resource type
findings.body: `getResourceName` only resolves human-readable names for the `Users` resource type. Since per-client resources are stored under the client's internal UUID (see `resolveClient`), permission representations for `Clients` permissions fall through to `resource.getDisplayName()`, which is not set for these generated resources and will therefore be null/empty in the admin REST responses and console, instead of the aggregate name ("All clients") or the client's clientId.

findings.title: Javadoc on void require* methods documents a return value
findings.body: `requireView()` (line 96-98) and `requireViewClientScopes()` (line 100-103) are `void` methods but their new Javadoc says "Returns {@code true} if {@link #canView()} returns {@code true}". They should state that a ForbiddenException is thrown when the corresponding can* method returns false, as done for the other require* methods. Also, the Javadoc of `canList()` (line 72-76) mentions `AdminRoles#QUERY_USERS`, which is unrelated to client listing and looks copy-pasted from the user evaluator.

findings.title: Dead code left over from copy/paste
findings.body: `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken)` is private and never referenced (the only caller would have been `canExchangeTo`, which now throws). Likewise the `logger` field, and the imports `Scope`, `ClientModelIdentity`, `DefaultEvaluationContext`, `EvaluationContext` and the static import of `AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE` are unused. This dead code suggests an incomplete copy from `ClientPermissions` and should be removed to avoid confusion about token-exchange support in V2.

findings.title: New Clients scope map-roles-client-scope is untested
findings.body: The schema now exposes six scopes for the `Clients` resource type, but the added tests only cover `manage`, `configure`, `view`, `map-roles` and `map-roles-composite`. There is no test for `map-roles-client-scope` (`canMapClientScopeRoles`), nor for the all-clients variants of `map-roles*`/`configure`, so regressions in those evaluation paths would go unnoticed.
